title: AT-SPI invalidation-signal fidelity census on the canonical GTK3 fixture
question: For each GTK3 semantic scope, does an AT-SPI event conservatively signal every relevant semantic change (no false negatives), so that event presence can invalidate known state? Or is it only a wake hint, or unusable? The fresh CUA observation (get_window_state / list_windows through the Driver) is the ground truth; the fixture's own state file is the cross-check oracle; events are only candidate invalidators.

fixture_change.gate: CUA_GTK3_CONTROL_FIFO (task mode only); acks in CUA_GTK3_CONTROL_ACK
fixture_change.adds_when_on: a single-selection list (Choice Alpha/Beta/Gamma), a 'Dynamic area' container, a 'Recreatable' button below the task controls; window default height 460; JSON command channel (noop, set_text, focus, select, toggle_check, add_child[order], remove_child, recreate, window_open, window_close) applied on the GTK main loop with CLOCK_MONOTONIC start/end acks; a 'control' object in the task state file
fixture_change.default_off_check: default_off_smoke.py: base vs modified fixture without the env, task and harness modes, Driver element digest / count / window size / tree_markdown / state keys identical (control D1)

environment.isolation: every command that executes code runs under bin/hostless; every GUI/Driver/gi command additionally inside cua-x11-session.sh with CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1 and CUA_SESSION_EXTRA_ENV="CUA_SESSION_ATSPI=1" (private Xvfb, private session bus, private at-spi-bus-launcher + at-spi2-registryd)
environment.listener: atspi_listener.py: system python3 + Gio only (no Gtk/Atk); connects to the private AT-SPI bus, subscribes to every broadcast signal (signal_subscribe with no filter) BEFORE registering object:, window:, focus:, document: with org.a11y.atspi.Registry.RegisterEvent; writes CLOCK_MONOTONIC arrival, sender bus name, object path, interface, member, detail/detail1/detail2/any_data; resolves sender -> pid asynchronously (GetConnectionUnixProcessID)
environment.listener_lifecycle: retained per block: spawned and ready BEFORE the target fixture starts, so it is registered before every mutation of the block; its subscription latency (internal + spawn-to-ready) and cleanup cost (DeregisterEvent + unsubscribe + close, and SIGTERM-to-exit) are recorded per block
environment.note_on_registration_masking: the Driver itself registers object events with the registry (shared AT-SPI connection), so in every block applications already emit object events for the Driver; the listener's own registration is therefore not the only reason apps emit. Window:/Focus:/Document: interest is the listener's own.

steps: fresh observation through the Driver (get_window_state include_screenshot:false on the target window; plus list_windows for window/process blocks) + read of the fixture state file
ONE known mutation (variant 1 = fixture control channel, the Driver is not the producer; variant 2 = the Driver acts)
collect events until mutation end + 1000 ms (QUIESCE, bounded, fixed)
fresh observation again + state file read
loop_per_mutation.event_window: [harness mutation start, mutation end + 1000 ms] on CLOCK_MONOTONIC; events before (incl. those caused by the before-observation's walk) and after (incl. the after-observation's walk) are excluded
loop_per_mutation.latency_reference: variant 1: the fixture's ack m_start (when the app began applying the command); harness-produced mutations: harness m_start; Driver actions: the harness clock just before call_tool (also reported relative to tool return)

text_v1.producer: fixture set_text on the 'Note' entry (unique value)
text_v1.L2: Object:TextChanged (any detail) or Object:PropertyChange accessible-value from the target bus name

text_v2.producer: Driver set_value on the Note element_token from the before-observation (unique value)

focus_v1.delta: obs: none available (get_window_state exposes no focus field on Linux; recorded as unobservable); oracle: control.focus
focus_v1.L2: Object:StateChanged:focused or Event.Focus:* from the target

focus_v2.producer: Driver press_key Tab, delivery_mode foreground (background Tab is refused: background_unavailable)

selection_v1.producer: fixture select_row rotating Alpha->Beta->Gamma (always a change)
selection_v1.L2: Object:SelectionChanged, Object:ActiveDescendantChanged or Object:StateChanged:selected from the target

selection_v2.producer: Driver click foreground on the next Choice row's element_token (a background click on a list row does not select: pilot)

checkbox_v2.producer: Driver click background on the I agree element_token (AT-SPI route)

child_add_pts.producer: fixture adds a 'Dynamic item N' button: pack, then show (the common GTK3 order)
child_add_pts.delta: obs: sorted (role,label) of all elements; oracle: control.dynamic

child_add_stp.producer: fixture adds an already shown button: show, then pack

child_remove_pts.producer: fixture destroys the last dynamic item (added pack-then-show in the same rep)
child_remove_pts.L2: Object:ChildrenChanged:remove or Object:StateChanged:defunct with detail1=1 from the target

child_remove_stp.producer: fixture destroys the last dynamic item (added show-then-pack in the same rep)

recreate.producer: fixture destroys 'Recreatable' and packs a new button with the same accessible name in the same slot
recreate.delta: obs: (role,label,frame) of Recreatable (expected UNCHANGED: label similarity is never identity proof); oracle: control.recreatable_generation (the identity change)
recreate.L2: removal of the old node: Object:ChildrenChanged:remove or Object:StateChanged:defunct=1 from the target; add-side naming (ChildrenChanged:add) reported separately

window_create.producer: fixture opens a second toplevel 'CuaTestHarness GTK3 Aux'
window_create.delta: obs: titles of the target pid in list_windows; oracle: control.aux_window
window_create.L2: Event.Window:Create or Object:ChildrenChanged:add on the app root from the target

window_destroy.L2: Event.Window:Destroy or Object:ChildrenChanged:remove on the app root from the target

exit_v1.producer: harness SIGTERM to the fixture it started, waitpid
exit_v1.delta: obs: get_window_state on the old pid/window errors (or 0 elements) and the task-window list changes; oracle: process reaped (exit rc)
exit_v1.L2: registry Object:ChildrenChanged:remove on /org/a11y/atspi/accessible/root naming the old target bus name, or bus NameOwnerChanged(old name -> '') (each also reported separately)

exit_v2.producer: Driver click background on the 'Exit' element_token

process_start.producer: harness spawns a new fixture (same env), done when the new pid publishes its state file
process_start.delta: obs: task-window list changes and the new window observes > 0 elements; oracle: state file published by the new pid
process_start.L2: registry Object:ChildrenChanged:add on the root naming the new target bus name, or NameOwnerChanged('' -> new name)

post_restart_probe.producer: fixture toggles 'I agree' in the restarted process

registry_restart.producer: harness SIGTERMs this session's at-spi2-registryd (started by this lane's own session script or by this harness) and relaunches /usr/lib/at-spi2-registryd --use-gnome-session (killing alone is not deterministic: the registry is not re-activated, and the Driver's observation then comes back empty; pilot)
registry_restart.delta: none expected (obs full digest + state seq); any event is a false-positive cost

post_registry_probe.producer: fixture toggles 'I agree' after the registry restart; evaluated with the RETAINED listener whose registration was held by the killed registry

noop.producer: fixture noop command (acked, no state change)
noop.delta: none expected (obs full digest + state seq)

decoy.producer: a lane-started second fixture process mutates itself (alternating toggle_check / set_text); the target is untouched
decoy.fp_split: unfiltered (any AT-SPI event) vs source-filtered (target bus name only)

listener_cycle.producer: a FRESH listener is spawned and becomes ready, then the fixture toggles 'I agree' immediately; evaluated with the fresh listener's events (the retained listener is the reference)
listener_cycle.timings: fresh listener subscription_ms, spawn_to_ready_ms, cleanup_ms, stop_to_exit_ms per rep

definitions.L1: any org.a11y.atspi.Event.* signal from the target's bus name in the window (process rows: any L2 lifecycle signal or target event)
definitions.L2: a scope-typed event that names the change type (per row above); sender identity = bus unique name resolved to the target pid, never a label
definitions.relevant_delta: observation delta OR oracle delta for the row's selected fields (focus: oracle only, because the observation has no focus field); both are recorded with their agreement
definitions.false_negative: a rep with a relevant delta and no L2 event in the window (FN_L2); FN_L1 = no target event at all
definitions.false_positive: a rep without a relevant delta that has an L1 target event (source-filtered) or any AT-SPI event (unfiltered); false positives are a performance cost only
definitions.spurious: per rep, target events in the window that are not L2 (e.g. BoundsChanged animation frames)

classification.inherited_meaning: the destroy/recreate and restart rows for an in-app scope: a known state is only safely invalidated by events if the node-destroy, process exit/start and post-restart/post-registry-restart cases also produce their invalidator
classification.rule: n = own reps with a relevant delta; fn2 = own FN_L2; fn1 = own FN_L1; inh = sum of FN_L2 over the inherited rows. n == 0 -> NO_DELTA_OBSERVED; fn2 == 0 and inh == 0 -> SAFE_INVALIDATOR (suffix _UNDERPOWERED if any own or inherited row has < 20 delta reps); else fn1/n < 0.25 -> NOISY_HINT (wakes a re-observation in >= 75% of own delta reps, but has a false negative or does not name the change); else UNUSABLE_ALWAYS_OBSERVE
classification.single_fn: a single relevant false negative (own or inherited) means event absence cannot authorize reuse for that scope
classification.finite_zero: SAFE_INVALIDATOR is a finite zero over n reps on this fixture/binary/session, not a universal guarantee
classification.recommendation: 'always observe' for every scope with any false negative; no observation-skipping policy is proposed for any scope (product invariant: no production observation skipping; events are wake hints, never the oracle, never authority)
classification.disposition_rule: #20 KEEP when the census is complete (every row attempted with >= 20 reps, every failure in the denominator) with the classification table and the recommendation; otherwise REVISE with what is missing

controls.noop: row noop (no semantic delta expected; target events = FP)
controls.decoy: row decoy (foreign events; FP unfiltered vs source-filtered)
controls.registry_restart_no_delta: row registry_restart (lifecycle signals without semantic delta)
controls.default_off: D1 default_off_smoke.py (fixture change inert without the env)
controls.obs_vs_oracle: every rep records observation delta and state-file delta; disagreement counted per row

not_run.chromium_electron: NOT_RUN. Gate recorded by chrome_atspi_probe.py (control G1): under the mandated bin/hostless (bwrap user namespace) root-owned files appear as uid 65534, so the Driver refuses to launch any system Chromium ('browser_route_unavailable: no root-owned, non-writable system Chromium executable is available for isolated launch'); no forbidden flag was used or is permitted, so Chrome's AT-SPI exposure in the private session cannot be tested here

timing_and_locks.per_block: each block runs as: hostless run_batch.sh -> bin/quiet-timed own20-<block_id> cua-x11-session.sh run_in_session.sh ... (EXCLUSIVE quiet-lane lock + ledger receipt); <= 10 measured mutations per acquisition
timing_and_locks.reported_timings: event-arrival latency (first L2, first L1, last target event) per row; fixture op duration; Driver call duration; listener subscription and cleanup (retained per block; fresh per listener_cycle rep); median, nearest-rank p95, min, max; every rep kept
timing_and_locks.loadavg: recorded per block (start/end) and per mutation; DISPLAY recorded per block
timing_and_locks.counts_only_blocks: D1 default-off smoke and G1 Chromium gate run under flock -s on the same lock with a receipt in raw/lock-ledger.jsonl

schedule.generator: schedule.py (round-robin over block types, order reversed on odd rounds)

pilots_uncounted.what: three exploratory probes and nine 1-2-rep pilot blocks of census.py, a default-off smoke pilot and two Chromium-gate pilots, all under hostless + the isolated session, before this file; none is counted
informed: element fields exposed by get_window_state on Linux (label, role, value, selected, enabled, frame, snapshot-scoped element_token; no focus field)

Driver variant-2 actions that land (background click on a check box via AT-SPI; set_value; foreground click selects a list row; foreground Tab moves focus); background click on a list row and background Tab do not
registry kill alone is not re-activated; kill + relaunch is deterministic
the add-order variants (pilots showed no ChildrenChanged:add for a pack-then-show child)
the session label required for browser_prepare
pilots_uncounted.expectations_from_pilots: child_add: no ChildrenChanged:add (L1 only via ancestor BoundsChanged); child_remove: defunct=1 on the removed node, no ChildrenChanged:remove for a child the container accessible never cached; other rows: typed events present. These are pilot observations (n <= 2), not results

claim_boundary: GTK3 fixture (task window + test-only control channel) on X11 Xvfb with a private AT-SPI bus and registry, at the tested source SHA and the r2-main-229b65b28 binary, Linux only. No other toolkit, no Chromium/Electron, no Wayland, no real desktop, no observation-skipping policy.
